description: A mark covers consuming the iterator it returns, so a returned iterator this rule cannot trace to a call is refused — unprovable is not clean. The two floors say which problem it is: a parameter is unknowable from here, a `let` is not analyzed yet.

diagnostics.message: This `@nothrow` function returns an iterator, so the mark covers consuming it too: nothing in the syntax names the call that produced it, so nothing can say whether consuming it throws. Your outs, in precedence order: return the iterator from a call this rule can trace — a direct call, or a `const` initialized by one; assert the producer's color in `nothrow.overrides.json`; install or write an `@nothrow/*` overlay; or, if you own the package, ship a manifest with `nothrow emit`.

This `@nothrow` function returns an iterator, so the mark covers consuming it too: it reaches here through a binding this rule does not follow yet — only a direct call, or a `const` initialized by one, traces to the call that produced it — so it is assumed to throw.
